AXP.rationale: AXP presents a moderately attractive fundamental-valuation setup. The franchise is durable — closed-loop network with 99% US merchant coverage, premium customer base spending 3-4x Visa/Mastercard levels, record $10B net card fees in FY2025 (+18% YoY), and 73% of new accounts on fee-paying products. Earnings trajectory is strong: EPS grew +17.6% YoY in Q1 2026 to $4.28, with revenue +9.3% YoY and ROE at 33%. The key valuation dislocation is that P/E has compressed to 19.5x — near the floor of its 12-month range (18.4-25.3x) and well below the Dec 2025 peak of 25.1x — even as fundamentals improved. This is multiple compression on an improving earnings base, not a value trap. Mean reversion to ~22x on annualized EPS (~$17.12, or management's guided $17.30-$17.90) implies ~18-25% upside. Berkshire's continued concentrated holding under new CEO Greg Abel provides institutional validation. Offsets tempering a higher score: (1) Q1 OCF declined -20.2% YoY to $3.80B, a meaningful deterioration warranting monitoring; (2) debt grew +14.7% YoY vs equity +8.9%, indicating rising leverage; (3) Q1 revenue came in 5.1% below analyst expectations per StockStory, creating near-term estimate uncertainty; (4) macro backdrop with 10Y at 4.45%, Baa at 6.0%, and jobless claims ticking to 230K poses consumer credit risk. The near-term catalyst is modest — management reaffirmed 9-10% revenue growth and $17.30-$17.90 EPS guidance, plus a $16B buyback authorization and 16% dividend hike — but the Q1 revenue miss tempers the re-rating urgency. Net: strong franchise + improving earnings + significant multiple compression = constructive, but OCF/leverage/watchpoints and the revenue miss cap conviction at moderately attractive rather than strongly so.
